Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 40-year-old woman with 3-week history of unilateral left hearing loss, facial numbness, tinnitus and episodic dizziness; no otalgia, discharge, fever, dysphagia, limb weakness, or visual symptoms. Past nasal polyps. Brother with NF.

Working diagnosis: Unilateral cranial nerve involvement—rule out acoustic/vestibular schwannoma vs idiopathic facial-nerve neuropathy (Bell’s palsy) or other CPA pathology.

Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):  
• Vestibular schwannoma (High likelihood): fits unilateral sensorineural loss, tinnitus, facial numbness, NF family history.  
• Idiopathic Bell’s palsy (Medium likelihood): clinician consideration, but sensory > motor findings and associated hearing loss make it less typical.  

Plan: Same-day face-to-face GP assessment for full neurological and otoscopic examination. Consider audiogram and MRI/IAC if exam suggests sensorineural loss or facial-nerve involvement. Provide reassurance that condition unlikely life-threatening but needs prompt evaluation.

Management Plan

- Arrange same-day in-clinic appointment for comprehensive neurological exam and otoscopy (admin team to schedule; patient to call support number).  
- Advise patient to attend today and seek urgent care if new neurological deficits arise.  
- Provide initial reassurance; explained that preliminary impression does not indicate life-threatening condition.  
- Discussed potential need for imaging (MRI internal auditory canal/brain) and audiology after in-person assessment.  
- No medications initiated at this telehealth visit.  
- Safety-net advice given.

1. Vestibular schwannoma (High) – unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, facial numbness, NF family history.  
2. Idiopathic Bell’s palsy (Medium) – unilateral facial sensory change; mentioned by clinician though presentation atypical.
